newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn may let business run parts of government.
newsitem.headline: Bonn may let business run parts of government.

text.p: The German Interior Ministry said on Monday that allowing private enterprise to run the business of government might be the best way to overcome the sluggishness of the country's bloated state bureacracy.

A spokesman said Interior Minister Manfred Kanther would present a proposal in February to shift administration of some state functions -- such as payroll accounting -- out of the hands of civil servants to private industry.
Kanther has been pressing to reform state administration for some time.
But any moves in this direction have met stiff opposition from the Federation of Civil Servants (DBB) and white-collar trade unions.
The DBB, responding to the new proposal, said it had no fundamental opposition to privatisation, but it did not believe this would make the government more efficient.
Herbert Mai, head of the Public Transport and Service Workers union (OeTV), said such a move would not save the government any money.
The government was just avoiding its responsibility to carry out genuine administrative reform, he said.
